title: Bound indexed column fail-closed ordering before a production change

finding.problem: GPU-37 validates indexed row keys before sorting, but indexed column keys still reach ordered.sort() before the canonical constructor validates column types. A mixed exact-integer/non-integer column set can therefore leak Python comparison TypeError instead of failing closed through the relation-block ValueError contract.
finding.risk: The canonical indexed owner is now used by verified Fourfold/Forest projections. Letting Python tuple ordering decide malformed-column behavior makes the internal boundary less deterministic and less fail-closed than its row side and persisted CSR contract.

probe.case: one valid (row=0,column=0) entry plus one (row=0,column='1') entry; require canonical ValueError before sorting
probe.result: negative evidence: multiple Python/hash contract arms had already failed in the integrated contract surface before the run was cancelled by the deliberate cleanup commit; isolated-wheel imports had succeeded

decision.next_bounded_change: In the existing TypedRelationBlock._from_indexed owner, validate every column key as an exact int within column-axis bounds before ordered.sort(), preserving the existing constructor as the final CSR/scalar validator. Pin mixed incomparable columns plus bool/float/string aliases and range failures without adding another builder or validator.

claim_boundaries.correctness: Negative PR-integration evidence for the indexed-column pre-sort validation gap only; no production fix is claimed in GPU-38.
